change: Only init content changes; diagnostic opt-in before core_mounts_ready
diagnostic_init:
#!/bin/busybox sh
# PID 1 of the sandbox guest image. Mounts the kernel filesystems, starts the
# guest agent, and leaves a shell on the console for whoever is debugging.
/bin/busybox --install -s /bin
mount -t proc proc /proc
mount -t sysfs sysfs /sys
mount -t devtmpfs devtmpfs /dev
# Opt-in kernel-timestamped milestones for cold-readiness investigations.
# The kernel passes unknown KEY=value command-line words to init's environment.
# Keep normal boots silent: each console byte adds an emulated UART exit.
boot_trace() {
    [ -n "$HV2_BOOT_TRACE" ] || return 0
    printf '<6>HV2_BOOT %s\n' "$1" >/dev/kmsg
}
export HV2_BOOT_TRACE=1
boot_trace core_mounts_ready
mkdir -p /dev/pts /etc /tmp /root
mount -t devpts devpts /dev/pts
mount -t tmpfs tmpfs /tmp

# The kernel configured the network from `ip=` on its command line and wrote
# the nameserver to /proc/net/pnp, which is in resolv.conf's own format.
[ -e /etc/resolv.conf ] || ln -s /proc/net/pnp /etc/resolv.conf
ip link set lo up 2>/dev/null

export PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin HOME=/root
# An image built from an OCI image carries that image's ENV here, so what the
# agent runs sees the environment the image was made for (its PATH first).
[ -f /etc/hv2-env ] && . /etc/hv2-env
boot_trace agent_launch
/bin/hv2-guest-agentd &
echo "=== HV2 READY ==="
exec setsid sh -c "exec sh </dev/console >/dev/console 2>&1"
